summary:
ASTRA HEALTH is an interactive, NASA-inspired spacecraft biomedical monitoring and health assessment prototype designed to support astronauts during long-duration missions to the International Space Station, the Moon, and Mars. Built using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Chart.js, and Three.js, the platform simulates a real-time spacecraft medical telemetry interface.
​Crew members can log and track critical vital signs—including blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, core body temperature, sleep duration, and psychological well-being—with all entries persisting locally via LocalStorage. A rule-based assessment engine evaluates measurements against contextual spaceflight ranges and personal baselines, classifying status levels into clear GREEN, YELLOW, and RED operational tiers. Beyond telemetry, ASTRA HEALTH features interactive 2D and 3D human body system mapping, longitudinal Chart.js analytics, educational modules covering NASA’s five major spaceflight hazards, a local biomedical guidance assistant, and daily wellness tracking to promote crew readiness and countermeasure compliance
details:
1. What It Does & What It Can Do

​ASTRA HEALTH is an interactive spacecraft biomedical telemetry and health assessment web application designed for astronauts on long-duration missions to the International Space Station (ISS), the Moon, and Mars.

​Live Vitals Telemetry & Logging: Allows crew members to log six core biomarkers—blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration, and psychological well-being—and compare them against historical records.

​Automated Risk Assessment: Evaluates entered vitals in real time and assigns clear operational status tiers (GREEN for nominal, YELLOW for repeat check/advisory, and RED for urgent flight surgeon protocols).

​Longitudinal Health Analytics: Visualizes health trends across 24-hour, 7-day, and 30-day windows using interactive charts and baseline comparison cards.

​Interactive 2D & 3D Human Anatomy: Lets users click through seven major physiological systems (nervous, cardiovascular, respiratory, skeletal, muscular, digestive, and immune) to inspect how microgravity and radiation affect each system.

​Mission Environment Switching: Adapts mission parameters, communication latency, radiation dose rates, and medical risk profiles dynamically between LEO (ISS), Lunar (0.16g), and Martian (0.38g) environments.

​Spaceflight Education & AI Guidance: Features an interactive module on NASA's five spaceflight hazards (RIDGE framework), a local rule-based biomedical guidance assistant, and a gamified daily countermeasure checklist.

​2. How It Works

​The application operates as a self-contained, client-side web platform requiring zero paid APIs or external servers:

​1. Data Persistence (LocalStorage): On initial load, the system generates a realistic 30-day simulated telemetry dataset. Whenever a user logs new vitals, completes wellness tasks, or updates crew baselines, the data is saved directly in the browser's localStorage so nothing is lost on refresh.

​2. Rule-Based Evaluation Engine: Custom JavaScript logic compares each incoming vital sign against both spaceflight-adapted operational bands and the individual astronaut's pre-flight baseline (e.g., accounting for plasma volume shifts and resting heart rate variations) before calculating a composite Flight Readiness Index.

​3. Dynamic Rendering: Updating any measurement automatically triggers a state recalculation that refreshes the Mission Overview, updates the six Chart.js graphs, recalculates wellness points, and feeds live telemetry into the local AI Health Assistant.

​3. Benefits & Intended Impact

​Key Benefits:

​Autonomous Crew Support: On deep-space missions to Mars where communication delays reach up to 44 minutes round-trip, astronauts cannot rely on real-time Earth telemedicine. ASTRA HEALTH demonstrates how onboard decision-support tools can guide immediate triage.

​Contextualized Space Medicine: Rather than applying standard Earth hospital thresholds, the system accounts for normal physiological adaptations to microgravity (such as cephalad fluid shifts and subclinical insulin resistance).

​Preventive Countermeasure Adherence: Gamifying hydration, resistive exercise (ARED), and sleep hygiene helps prevent bone density loss and muscle atrophy before they become critical.

​Intended Impact: To bridge the gap between complex space medicine research and usable spacecraft software—empowering both crew members and students/researchers to understand how human physiology adapts to deep space while reinforcing safe, human-in-the-loop medical protocols.

​4. Coding Platform & Technology Stack

​Development Environment: Built and tested in Visual Studio Code (VS Code) using the Live Server extension for local HTTP hosting and browser developer tools for debugging.

​Core Languages & Libraries:

​HTML5 & CSS3: Semantic structure and a custom NASA-inspired dark-navy glassmorphism UI with responsive CSS Grid/Flexbox layouts.

​Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+): Modular state management, validation, local rule-based Q&A logic, and assessment algorithms.

​Chart.js: Dynamic, responsive multi-timeframe line and bar telemetry charts.

​Three.js: Interactive 3D wireframe biometric mesh alongside a custom 2D vector SVG anatomy map.

​Lucide Icons: Clean, technical aerospace iconography.

​5. How Your Project Is Creative

​Mission-Aware Medical Logic: Unlike standard fitness or health trackers that assume a fixed environment on Earth, ASTRA HEALTH lets users toggle between 0g (ISS), 0.16g (Moon), and 0.38g (Mars)—changing radiation rates, evacuation windows, communication delays, and medical risk profiles on the fly.

​Dual-Mode Anatomical Exploration: Combining an interactive 2D SVG organ hotspot map with a rotatable 3D Three.js telemetry mesh turns dense NASA Human Research Program physiology into an intuitive visual experience.

​Offline-First Spacecraft Realism: Designing the AI guidance assistant and telemetry engine to run completely locally mimics the real-world constraints of deep-space computing, where constant cloud connectivity does not exist.

​6. Key Factors Your Team Considered

​Medical Safety & Ethical Guardrails: Your team explicitly avoided designing an autonomous diagnostic or prescribing tool. Every alert prioritizes repeat measurements, sensor verification, and escalating to a Flight Surgeon, backed by clear disclaimers distinguishing simulated telemetry from clinical advice.

​Spaceflight Physiological Accuracy: Grounded the educational content and reference ranges in NASA's RIDGE hazards framework (Radiation, Isolation, Distance, Gravity, Hostile/Closed Environments), addressing real spaceflight conditions like SANS (vision changes) and bone mineral loss.

​Usability Under High-Stress Conditions: Prioritized clean visual hierarchy, color-coded status tiers (Green/Yellow/Red), rapid single-tap logging modals, and keyboard/screen-reader accessibility so critical health data can be read within seconds.

​Zero-Dependency Reliability: Engineered the entire prototype to run offline without paid API keys or backend servers, ensuring reliable demonstrations anywhere.
